transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling really bad about myself lately. Like, I keep thinking I’m a disappointment, and… I don’t know if this sounds dramatic, but there was this near-miss, and I can’t stop feeling like it proves I’m dangerous or not meant to be a nurse. I keep thinking everyone might be better off without me.
Have you had similar feelings before, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

It’s… not exactly the first time. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I think it’s been kind of on and off for about a year or so—maybe a year and two months. It started after I graduated high school, when I began college classes and working full-time at the clinic. I thought I was just adjusting badly, if that makes sense.
Have these feelings of sadness or low self-worth been present most of the time, nearly every day, for at least two years?

No… I don’t think it’s been two years. It’s been more like a little over a year—about a year and two months, I guess. It started after I graduated high school and began taking college classes while working full-time at the clinic. I hope that makes sense.
Has your mood been consistently low or depressed most of the time, nearly every day, for at least the past two years?

I don’t think it’s been two full years, no. But… most days I do wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I try to act normal at the clinic—like smiling at patients, even in Spanish—and I can usually make it look okay, I think. But inside it feels like I’m barely holding myself together. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you experienced these low or depressed moods for at least two years, or has it been for a shorter duration?

It’s been shorter than two years. I know I’ve said it a few times, sorry… it’s more like about a year and two months. It started after I graduated high school and was trying to do college classes while working full-time at the clinic. I thought maybe I was just not handling the change very well.
Have you had days where your mood was so low or depressed that it felt like you couldn’t go on, and if so, how long have you been feeling this way?

Um… yeah, I guess I have had days like that. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself or anything, I really don’t. It’s more like… sometimes I keep thinking it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up, or if I could just disappear so I wouldn’t mess anything up again.

I’m sorry, that sounds bad. I’ve been feeling that on and off for… probably around this past year or so, maybe a little over a year. Is that what you mean?
Do these low or depressed feelings tend to last most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can still get through work and smile at patients, even speak Spanish with them and seem normal, so it’s not like I’m crying all day or anything. But most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, and it kind of stays there. Even when I’m acting okay at the clinic, inside I feel like I’m just barely holding myself together. Is that… the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have your low or depressed feelings been present for at least two years, or has it been for a shorter duration?

It’s been shorter than two years… I’m sorry, I know I already mentioned it. It’s been about a year and two months, I think. It started after I graduated high school, when I was trying to do college classes and work full-time at the clinic. I thought at first it was just stress or me not adjusting well.
Just to be clear, have these low or depressed feelings been happening most of the time for at least two years, or has it been less than that?

Less than that, yeah. Sorry, I know I’m repeating myself — I just want to be clear. It’s been about a year and two months, not two years. It really started after I graduated high school and was trying to handle college classes while working full-time at the clinic.
Have your low or depressed feelings been happening most of the time for at least two years, or has it been less than that?

It’s less than two years. I know I’ve said it a few times, sorry — I just don’t want to answer wrong. It’s been about a year and two months, since after I graduated high school and started trying to do college classes while working full-time at the clinic.
Have there been any periods lasting at least two months during this past year and two months where you felt completely free of these low or depressed feelings?

I don’t think there’s been a full two months where it was completely gone, no. It’s been kind of there since after graduation, when I started college classes and working full-time at the clinic… about a year and two months now. Some times have been better than others, but I wouldn’t say I was totally free of it for that long.
After your first period of feeling this way, did you have a time when you felt significantly better for at least several weeks before these feelings came back again?

I’m not totally sure how to separate it, honestly. I don’t remember a clear stretch of several weeks where I felt really significantly better and then it came back. There were times I was more okay, I guess, but not like… back to myself for weeks. Does that answer it the way you mean?

Before this current period of feeling low, which started about a year and two months ago, had you ever experienced a time when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I don’t think so… I mean, I had normal bad days in high school and stuff, but I don’t remember anything before this where it was most of the day, almost every day for two weeks. At least not that I would’ve called depressed. Is that helpful?
During the past year and two months, has there been a time when your low or depressed feelings completely went away for at least two months?

No, I don’t think it ever completely went away for two months. It’s been there to some degree since after I graduated high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic… so, about a year and two months now. Some days are better, but not fully gone like that.
